plan.estimand: Minimum total development sample size for binary clinical prediction model meeting Riley criteria precision specifications
plan.hypothesis: Sample size sufficient to achieve target apparent-versus-adjusted R-squared difference (Nagelkerke) of 0.05 or less and outcome-risk margin of error of 0.05

parameters.name: Precision criterion: maximum apparent-versus-adjusted R-squared difference (Nagelkerke)
Target average outcome-risk absolute margin of error

assumptions: pmsampsize 1.1.3 package default precision criteria apply
Riley criteria methodology for prediction model sample size
Outcome prevalence represents marginal distribution in development sample
clarification_questions: Confirming: the target margin of error of 0.05 refers to the absolute width of the 95% confidence interval for average predicted outcome risk (outcome probability), correct?
scientific_notes: Riley et al. (2015) criteria balance model overfitting (apparent-adjusted R-squared difference) with precision of average predicted risk
Cox-Snell R-squared converted to Nagelkerke scale internally by pmsampsize for binary models
Shrinkage 0.90 represents anticipated moderate-to-good model calibration post-development
pmsampsize documentation specifies precision as 95% CI half-width requirement by default
